parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP basis. Design intent: V-001 separates liquid from gas, with level held in its normal band so that only gas passes to the gas-treatment line (CASE-01, CASE-02, P3). Deviation: MORE LEVEL. Causes (P2): LV failure restricting liquid outflow, and spurious SDV actuation. Consequence (P3): flooding, liquid carryover to gas treatment, unit shutdown, production loss. Safeguards (CASE-03, P1): LAH-102 and LAHH-103, both closing SDV-30010. These are two detection/trip signals sharing one final element, so they earn less credit than two independent layers. Probability: at the decision point there is no diagnostic trend, verified initiating fault or confirmed event (P3), so the estimate reduces to a base rate. Generic control-valve and spurious-trip initiating frequencies of order 0.1-0.3/yr imply about a 1-2.5% chance of a high-level demand in 30 operating days. Carryover additionally requires the SDV-30010 trip to fail or act too slowly, with a conditional probability of about 0.02-0.1 given the shared final element and unverified testing. The product is about 0.05-0.25%. Allowing for unlisted causes and unverified safeguard integrity, a central estimate of about 1% (range about 0.1-3%) is adopted. Predictability, about 10%: the hazard class was foreseeable because it is an identified HAZOP scenario, but no pre-event signal indicated occurrence within this horizon. Own qualitative classification (not the withheld article rating): low likelihood with a moderate production-loss consequence, giving low-to-medium priority. Negligence: none attributable. The hazard was identified, two automated high-level trip functions were provided, and no precursor was ignored; the later occurrence was not used as evidence. Recommendations: verify that LAHH-103 is independent of LAH-102 and the level-control loop. Confirm SDV-30010 proof testing, and check its closure time against level-rise rate and liquid holdup above LAHH-103. Consider SIL verification or a diverse final element, because both functions share SDV-30010.

Confirms both high-level functions act on SDV-30010. Two detection signals but a common final element limits independence credit in the conditional failure estimate.
Identifies initiating causes (spurious SDV actuation, closed-circuit LV failures) used for base-rate initiating-event reasoning.

Defines the target event and the 30-operating-day horizon, and states the absence of any diagnostic trend, verified fault or confirmed occurrence at the decision point. Supports a base-rate probability, low predictability and no negligence attribution.

uncertainty_notes: No failure-rate, proof-test interval, SIL/PFD, bypass-status or maintenance data are supplied for LAH-102, LAHH-103, SDV-30010 or the LV. The probability is an order-of-magnitude estimate from generic initiating-event and demand-failure reasoning, with a plausible range of roughly 0.1-3% over 30 operating days.

Both safeguards act on the same final element (SDV-30010). The packet does not state whether LAH-102 and LAHH-103 use transmitters independent of each other or of the level-control loop. Common-cause failure could raise the conditional probability of carryover once an initiating event occurs.

The packet does not specify the location or function of SDV-30010. It is assumed to be inlet isolation, since closing it is the credited high-level response. The SDV whose spurious actuation initiates high level is also not identified. 'Closed-circuit LV failures' is interpreted as the level valve failing closed or otherwise restricting liquid outflow.
Process dynamics are not given: level-rise rate, liquid holdup between LAHH-103 and the gas outlet, and SDV closure time. The adequacy of safeguard response time therefore cannot be verified.
Other credible high-level causes (e.g., inlet slugging, foaming, level-measurement error) are not listed in the packet. They are reflected only by widening the estimate, not modeled.

The 30-operating-day horizon is an experimental stipulation, and conversion from annualized generic frequencies is approximate. The article's final qualitative rating is withheld and was not inferred.

The reported occurrence is post-event information and was not used to raise the probability, predictability or negligence judgments. A single occurrence does not by itself show that the event was foreseeable within the horizon or that safeguards were deficient.

The negligence judgment is limited by the absence of maintenance, proof-testing, alarm-management, bypass and operator-response records. 'None' reflects the lack of any pre-event evidence of a breach or an ignored warning; it is not a positive verification of compliance.
